description: The SELECT row-limiting and star-modifier surface, measured statement by statement against a real account (40 cells, whose verdicts agreed fully). Every part of the ANSI FETCH is optional except the count, so FETCH 2, FETCH FIRST 2, FETCH NEXT 2 ROWS ONLY and FETCH FIRST 2 ROW ONLY are one clause. OFFSET n [ROWS] may PREFIX a fetch but never stand alone - bare OFFSET stays a syntax error with or without ROWS. LIMIT '' and OFFSET '' are the documented empty-string defaults (they mean no limit / no offset) while any OTHER string refuses AT THE LITERAL, quoting it doubled in the message. The star modifiers come in ONE order - ILIKE-or-EXCLUDE, then REPLACE, then RENAME - each at most once, and ILIKE and EXCLUDE are mutually exclusive, so every wrong order is a syntax error naming the token that arrived too late. And TOP beside a LIMIT or a FETCH refuses with 'Duplicate LIMIT: <keyword>.', naming which one it found second. Converted 1:1 from query/SelectModifierSurfaceTest (now retired); two of its assertions compared the WHOLE message including the newline after the header, and those are pinned verbatim here.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE sm_t (a INTEGER, b INTEGER, c VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO sm_t VALUES (1, 10, 'x'), (2, 20, 'y'), (3, 30, 'z')
SELECT a FROM sm_t FETCH 2
SELECT a FROM sm_t FETCH FIRST 2
SELECT a FROM sm_t FETCH NEXT 2 ROWS ONLY
SELECT a FROM sm_t FETCH FIRST 2 ROW ONLY
CREATE TABLE sm_t (a INTEGER, b INTEGER, c VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO sm_t VALUES (1, 10, 'x'), (2, 20, 'y'), (3, 30, 'z')
SELECT a FROM sm_t ORDER BY a OFFSET 1 ROWS FETCH NEXT 2 ROWS ONLY
SELECT a FROM sm_t ORDER BY a OFFSET 2 FETCH 5
CREATE TABLE sm_t (a INTEGER, b INTEGER, c VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO sm_t VALUES (1, 10, 'x'), (2, 20, 'y'), (3, 30, 'z')
SELECT a FROM sm_t OFFSET 1
SELECT a FROM sm_t OFFSET 1 ROWS
CREATE TABLE sm_t (a INTEGER, b INTEGER, c VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO sm_t VALUES (1, 10, 'x'), (2, 20, 'y'), (3, 30, 'z')
SELECT a FROM sm_t LIMIT ''
SELECT a FROM sm_t LIMIT '' OFFSET ''
SELECT a FROM sm_t ORDER BY a LIMIT 2 OFFSET ''
CREATE TABLE sm_t (a INTEGER, b INTEGER, c VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO sm_t VALUES (1, 10, 'x'), (2, 20, 'y'), (3, 30, 'z')
SELECT a FROM sm_t LIMIT '3'

error.messageContains:
SQL compilation error:
syntax error line 1 at position 25 unexpected ''3''.

steps.sql: SELECT a FROM sm_t LIMIT 'abc'
CREATE TABLE sm_t (a INTEGER, b INTEGER, c VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO sm_t VALUES (1, 10, 'x'), (2, 20, 'y'), (3, 30, 'z')
SELECT * EXCLUDE c FROM sm_t
SELECT * EXCLUDE c RENAME a AS x FROM sm_t
SELECT * REPLACE (a + 1 AS a) RENAME b AS y FROM sm_t
SELECT * RENAME a AS x EXCLUDE c FROM sm_t
SELECT * RENAME b AS y REPLACE (a + 1 AS a) FROM sm_t
SELECT * EXCLUDE a EXCLUDE b FROM sm_t
CREATE TABLE sm_t (a INTEGER, b INTEGER, c VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO sm_t VALUES (1, 10, 'x'), (2, 20, 'y'), (3, 30, 'z')
SELECT * ILIKE 'a%' FROM sm_t
SELECT * ILIKE 'a%' EXCLUDE b FROM sm_t
SELECT * EXCLUDE a ILIKE 'b%' FROM sm_t
CREATE TABLE sm_t (a INTEGER, b INTEGER, c VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO sm_t VALUES (1, 10, 'x'), (2, 20, 'y'), (3, 30, 'z')
SELECT TOP 2 a FROM sm_t
SELECT TOP 2 a FROM sm_t LIMIT 1

Duplicate LIMIT: LIMIT.
